Paragraph:
Translation: The Vedas mainly deal with the subject of the three modes of material nature. Rise above these modes, O Arjuna. Be transcendental to all of them. Be free from all dualities and from all anxieties for gain and safety, and be established in the Self.

Purport (Excerpt): All material activities involve actions and reactions in the three modes of material nature... One has to learn tolerance in the face of dualities such as happiness and distress, or cold and warmth, and by tolerating such dualities become free from anxieties regarding gain and loss. This transcendental position is achieved in full Krsna consciousness...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is suffering from profound anxiety regarding 'gain and safety' (winning the kingdom vs. losing his family, securing his physical and moral safety).
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna instructs Arjuna to transcend the basic operating system of the material world (the three modes of nature). He commands him to tolerate dualities (hot/cold, joy/sorrow) and drop the exhausting anxiety over acquiring things (gain) and protecting them (safety).
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is given the pathway to absolute psychological freedom: anchoring himself in the eternal Self rather than the fluctuating material modes.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Anxiety Management: Becoming free from the constant worries of 'gain and safety'
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Tolerance of Discomfort: Accepting the inevitable dualities of life without losing equilibrium
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Letting Go of Control: Releasing the stressful need to perfectly manage material outcomes

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Traigunya (The three modes of material nature: goodness, passion, and ignorance)
Yoga-ksema (The anxiety of acquiring what one lacks and preserving what one has)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The material world operates under three modes (gunas) which constantly generate dualities and anxieties. Even basic Vedic rituals operate within this realm. Krishna urges Arjuna to become a transcendentalist (Nirguna)—to rise above this mechanical nature, tolerate its temporary fluctuations, and anchor his consciousness firmly in the eternal soul.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is a profound blueprint for overcoming generalized anxiety. Much of human anxiety stems from two things: chasing what we don't have ('gain') and terrified of losing what we do have ('safety'). Krishna teaches that by accepting the natural ups and downs of life (dualities) and grounding our identity in our unchangeable core ('established in the Self'), we can become completely immune to these exhausting anxieties.
